content:
Apple has updated its list of vintage and obsolete products today, adding the 15-inch MacBook Pro and iPhone X from 2018 to the obsolete list. Here's what that means.

The iPhone X and the 15-inch 2018 MacBook Pro are now classified as obsolete products.

Apple today updated a support article titled "Obtaining service for your Apple product after the warranty has expired," moving the 2018 15-inch MacBook Pro and iPhone X from the vintage list to the obsolete list.

Apple explains that once a product is added to the obsolete list, the company will discontinue all hardware repair services, and service providers will no longer be able to order parts for them.

Products may be classified as obsolete more than seven years after Apple stops selling them, but the actual timing of the classification is ultimately at Apple's discretion.

As for the vintage list, it includes products for which Apple only provides repairs while parts remain in stock. Apple defines products that it stopped selling more than five years but less than seven years ago as vintage products.

Apple has already ended main OS support for the iPhone X starting with iOS 17, with iOS 16 being its last major version; the device now supports up to iOS 16.7.16 at most. The 2018 15-inch MacBook Pro can only run up to macOS Sequoia, and the model currently offers up to macOS 15.7.7.

To view Apple's complete list of vintage and obsolete products, as well as cases where repair service for some products can be extended for up to 10 years, you can follow this link.
